answer_contract.answer: Energy-releasing reactions to energy-requiring cellular work.

locator.evidence_quote: ATP couples energy-releasing reactions to energy-requiring cellular work.

questions.explanation: ATP functions to link exergonic (energy-releasing) reactions with endergonic (energy-requiring) cellular processes so that the energy released by one drives the other.
questions.prompt: What does ATP couple in cells?

answer_contract.answer: By hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and phosphate, which can transfer energy to coupled processes.

locator.evidence_quote: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and phosphate can transfer energy to coupled processes.

questions.explanation: Breaking the terminal phosphate bond of ATP releases energy; the hydrolysis products (ADP and inorganic phosphate) are formed while the released energy is used to drive an otherwise unfavorable cellular reaction.
questions.prompt: How does hydrolysis of ATP transfer energy to other cellular processes?

answer_contract.answer: Because ATP is regenerated rather than stored as a long-term energy reserve.

locator.evidence_quote: ATP is regenerated rather than stored as a long-term energy reserve.

questions.explanation: Cells continually recycle ADP back to ATP through metabolic processes instead of storing large amounts of ATP, so ATP serves as a short-term energy carrier rather than a long-term storage molecule.
questions.prompt: Why is ATP not used as a long-term energy storage molecule?
